skills.name: test

skills.name: troubleshooting

skills.name: user-app-development

167. impl Address for PhysicalAddress {
168.     ///
169.     /// # Description
170.     ///
171.     /// Instantiates a new [`PhysicalAddress`] from a raw value.
172.     ///
173.     /// # Parameters
174.     ///
175.     /// - `raw_addr`: The raw value.
176.     ///
177.     /// # Returns
178.     ///
179.     /// - `Ok(Self)`: The new address.
180.     /// - `Err(Error::BadAddress)`: If the provided address is invalid.
181.     ///
182.     fn from_raw_value(value: usize) -> Result<Self, Error> {
183.         Self::from_virtual_address(VirtualAddress::from_raw_value(value))
184.     }
185. 
186.     ///
187.     /// # Description
188.     ///
189.     ///  Aligns the target [`PhysicalAddress`] to the provided `alignment`. If the address is already
190.     ///  aligned, it is returned as is.
191.     ///
192.     /// # Parameters
193.     ///
194.     /// - `alignment`: The alignment to align the target address to.
195.     ///
196.     /// # Returns
197.     ///
198.     /// Upon success, the aligned address is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
199.     ///
200.     fn align_up(&self, align: Alignment) -> Result<Self, Error> {
201.         let aligned: VirtualAddress = self.0.align_up(align).ok_or_else(|| {
202.             let reason: &str = "align_up overflow";
203.             error!(
204.                 "PhysicalAddress::align_up(): {reason} (addr={:#x}, align={:?})",
205.                 self.0.into_raw_value(),
206.                 align
207.             );
208.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason)
209.         })?;
210.         Self::from_virtual_address(aligned)
211.     }
212. 
213.     ///
214.     /// # Description
215.     ///
216.     /// Aligns the target [`PhysicalAddress`] down to the provided `alignment`. If the address is
217.     /// already aligned, it is returned as is.
218.     ///
219.     /// # Parameters
220.     ///
221.     /// - `alignment`: The alignment to align the target address to.
222.     ///
223.     /// # Returns
224.     ///
225.     /// Upon success, the aligned address is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
